content:
thought
The Anthracnose reference image `Mango_Leaf_14.jpg` shows a young, brownish leaf with significant damage, including holes and torn edges. This doesn't strongly resemble the test image, which has distinct, darker brown lesions on a green leaf.

Now I will view a reference image for Die_Back.

thought
The Die_Back reference image `Mango_Leaf_166.jpg` shows a completely dried, shriveled brown leaf. This is quite different from the test image, which has localized lesions on an otherwise green leaf.

Next, I will view a reference image for Powdery_Mildew.

thought
The Powdery_Mildew reference image `Mango_Leaf_14.jpg` shows a leaf covered in a white, powdery fungal growth. This is clearly different from the brown lesions seen in the test image.

Finally for the first round, I will view a reference image for Sooty_Mould.

thought
The Sooty_Mould reference image `Mango_Leaf_147.jpg` shows a leaf with dark, patchy, superficial fungal growth, which aligns with the symptom description of "dark, superficial fungal deposits". While the test image has brown lesions rather than black sooty growth, the irregular shape and surface nature of the lesions in the test image could potentially be an early stage or a different manifestation of sooty mould. However, it's not a perfect match.

Let's revisit Anthracnose as the initial reference image was of a very young leaf. The symptom description for Anthracnose mentions "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out." The test image has irregular brown spots. I will view another Anthracnose reference image.

thought
The Anthracnose reference image `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` shows distinct, dark brown to black, irregular spots on a green leaf. These spots are very similar in appearance and distribution to the lesions in the test image, although the test image spots appear slightly lighter brown. The description "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out" also aligns well. This is a much better match than the previous Anthracnose image and the images for Die_Back and Powdery_Mildew.

I will continue to explore other classes to use my full budget and ensure the best match. I'll look at another Sooty Mould image to compare further.

thought
The Sooty_Mould reference image `Mango_Leaf_164.jpg` shows a leaf with dark, brownish-black, irregular patches, more like a stain or coating than distinct spots. This is also a possible match, but `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` (Anthracnose) has a more similar "spot" pattern to the test image.

Let's look at another Anthracnose image to further confirm.

thought
This Anthracnose reference image (`Mango_Leaf_462.jpg`) shows a heavily damaged leaf, almost skeletal, which is not a good match for the test image. This image is labeled as 'pod' in the path, but clearly shows a leaf. I should have been more careful about the file path.

I have used 6 of my 16 image views. I will focus on comparing Anthracnose and Sooty_Mould further, as they seem to be the closest candidates.

Let me view another Die_Back image, but focus on a leaf image if possible to be sure. It seems `Mango_Leaf_444.jpg` is a leaf for Die_Back and Powdery_Mildew. Let me check the Die_Back one first.

thought
This Die_Back reference image (`Mango_Leaf_444.jpg`) is again of a completely dried and shriveled leaf, which is not consistent with the test image.

Now I will view another Powdery_Mildew image, `Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`.

thought
This Powdery_Mildew reference image `Mango_Leaf_164.jpg` also shows white, powdery spots, consistent with powdery mildew, but not the brown lesions of the test image.

So far, Anthracnose `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` is the best match. I've used 8 views. I have 8 views remaining.

I will view the last Sooty_Mould image (`Mango_Leaf_288.jpg`) to make a final comparison between Anthracnose and Sooty_Mould.

thought
The Sooty_Mould reference image `Mango_Leaf_288.jpg` shows a leaf with scattered dark spots and a general sooty appearance. While it has some spots, they are darker and more uniformly black/dark grey compared to the browner, more irregular lesions in the test image.

Comparing `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` (Anthracnose) and the test image, the shape, irregular edges, and distribution of the brown lesions are very similar. The color in the test image is slightly lighter brown than the dark spots in `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`, but the overall pattern is a much closer visual match than any of the Sooty_Mould images. The symptom description for Anthracnose, "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out," also fits the test image well, considering the browning could be a stage of the "black" spots or a variation.

I have used 9 views. I have 7 views left. I will now use the remaining views on Anthracnose as it is the closest match, to solidify my confidence. I will check any remaining Anthracnose leaf images.
There are no more Anthracnose leaf images in the provided list. I have already seen `Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`, `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`, and the `pod/Mango_Leaf_462.jpg` which was a leaf.

I must use all 16 views. Since Anthracnose is the best fit, I will use the remaining views on other Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, and Sooty_Mould images, even though they seem less likely, to ensure I've exhausted all options and used my budget.

Let me review another Powdery_Mildew image, `Mango_Leaf_444.jpg`.

thought
This Powdery_Mildew reference image `Mango_Leaf_444.jpg` also shows the characteristic white, powdery patches, which are distinctly different from the brown lesions in the test image.

I have used 10 views. I have 6 views remaining. I will continue to view all remaining images.

Next, I'll view the Die_Back stem image.

thought
This image `Mango_Leaf_147.jpg` is a dried-up brown leaf, not a stem, and also not a match for the test image. It seems the file path's `stem` directory does not always contain stem images.

I have used 11 views. I have 5 views remaining.

I have viewed all provided reference images for Anthracnose (leaf images), Die_Back (leaf images), Powdery_Mildew (leaf images), and Sooty_Mould (leaf images). The Anthracnose image `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` remains the most visually similar to the test image.

Since I must use all 16 views, and I have already seen all relevant images that are available, I will re-examine the Anthracnose images, and then fill the remaining budget by re-examining the Sooty_Mould images as those were the second closest.

Re-examining `Mango_Leaf_14.jpg` for Anthracnose (the first one I viewed).

thought
This Anthracnose `Mango_Leaf_14.jpg` image still does not resemble the test image.

Re-examining `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` for Anthracnose. This was the best match so far.

thought
This Anthracnose `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` image still remains the closest visual match to the test image, with similar irregular, dark spots on a green leaf.

I have used 13 views. I have 3 views left. I will re-examine the Sooty_Mould images to be absolutely sure.

Re-examining `Mango_Leaf_147.jpg` for Sooty_Mould.

thought
This Sooty_Mould `Mango_Leaf_147.jpg` image shows a general sooty, dark appearance, which is not the distinct spotting seen in the test image.

Re-examining `Mango_Leaf_164.jpg` for Sooty_Mould.

The Sooty_Mould `Mango_Leaf_164.jpg` shows irregular brownish-black patches that look more like a coating than distinct spots, still not as close as Anthracnose.

I have used 15 views. I have 1 view left.

Re-examining `Mango_Leaf_288.jpg` for Sooty_Mould to complete the budget.
